column3: The Hebrew repeats the upward direction in David’s second question and leaves the final respondent unnamed; BSB supplies the LORD.
The Hebrew explicitly says David went up and calls Abigail Nabal’s wife; BSB leaves the ascent implicit and calls her his widow.
The Hebrew explicitly says David brought his men up and calls their dwellings “the cities of Hebron”; BSB uses “towns near Hebron.”
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat Hebron as the men’s destination.
The Hebrew introduces David’s words with “and he said to them”; BSB turns them into the purpose of sending messengers.
The Hebrew says “this good” and “this thing”; BSB uses “the same favor” and “this.”
The Hebrew retains the images of strengthened hands and “sons of valor”; BSB says “be strong and courageous.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the Ashurites; BSB has Asher.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the period as the “number of days.”
The Hebrew contains no separate introductory “One day.”
The Hebrew says the groups sat on either side of the pool and repeats “the pool”; BSB calls this taking positions.
The Hebrew says the young men should “play”; BSB renders this as “compete.”
The Hebrew explicitly calls David’s twelve his servants.
The Hebrew describes the sword in the opponent’s side without a separate verb for thrusting. It has an unnamed singular subject naming the place; BSB uses passive “is called.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew compares his speed to one of the gazelles in the field.
The Hebrew repeats Abner’s name at the end; BSB uses “in his pursuit.”
The Hebrew leaves the respondent unnamed; BSB identifies him as Asahel.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says Abner spoke again; BSB specifies that he warned Asahel. It preserves lifting the face, where BSB uses “show my face.”
The Hebrew leaves the refusing man unnamed, repeats the spear as the object emerging, and states falling and dying separately. BSB names Asahel and uses “it came out” and “fell dead.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew speaks of gathering “behind Abner” and uses “sons of Benjamin”; BSB has “rallied to Abner” and “Benjamites.”
The Hebrew calls the listeners “the people”; BSB specifies “the troops.”
The Hebrew says that without Abner’s words the people would have withdrawn “from the morning”; BSB says they would have continued pursuing until morning.
The Hebrew calls the people “all the people”; BSB specifies “all the troops.”
The Hebrew says they went through all Bithron; BSB says they marched all morning.
The Hebrew joins Asahel to the nineteen men with “and”; BSB uses “In addition to.”
